_marker: THE DENOMINATOR. Hand-authored per case, generated into one index. Deliberately NOT derived from isFusable / styled / DECLARED_CHANNELS / CHANNEL_TO_COMPUTED / TOKEN_CHANNELS / carriedParts — every instrument in the pipeline derives its denominator from the same filter that decides carriage, which is why a channel the filter never opened scores 100%. This file is the independent one.

cases.construct: accent-color: rebeccapurple on a native checkbox
cases.why: The one-line way to theme native form controls; it is the ONLY paint the control has.

canvas.note: the checked box fill is real ink

cases.why: Media thumbnails and avatars. A declared ratio the browser resolves into a real box.

canvas.note: fixed w/h frame

cases.why: Frosted-glass headers and sheets. Figma has BACKGROUND_BLUR — also canvas-expressible.

canvas.note: Figma BACKGROUND_BLUR is an exact match

cases.why: Corner radius is a first-class Figma property and a first-class token.

canvas.note: cornerRadius

cases.why: Elevation. A single shadow is the one effect shape Figma maps 1:1 (DROP_SHADOW).

canvas.note: DROP_SHADOW effect

cases.why: Density scales are computed, not literal. calc() over a token is how every compact mode ships.

canvas.note: the resolved px is right; the token name is at risk

cases.why: Ribbons, notched cards, sr-only insets. clip-path decides what is VISIBLE.

canvas.note: arbitrary polygon clipping has no frame-level spelling

cases.why: Hex is the spelling designers use; the browser normalises it to rgb() and the mint must agree.

canvas.note: text fill

cases.why: The baseline paint channel. Every fill in every library reduces to this.

canvas.note: SOLID fill

cases.why: Hover overlays and scrims are alpha fills; alpha must survive the mint as an 8-digit hex.

canvas.note: SOLID fill with opacity

cases.why: Container queries are how 2026-era libraries do responsive components. The rule MATCHES here.

canvas.note: a size-conditional rendering is a MODE, not a single canvas variant

cases.why: Long virtualised lists opt out of rendering; an off-screen subtree has NO computed geometry.

canvas.note: a rendering optimisation, not ink

cases.why: Semantic-over-primitive token layering is TWO hops; the reader follows exactly one.

canvas.note: the pixel is right; the NAME is what is at risk

cases.why: RTL INVERTS the physical meaning of every logical property — the exact pin LOGICAL_ALIASES rests on.

canvas.note: Figma AutoLayout does have RTL; and if the alias pin does not invert, the padding lands on the WRONG side

cases.why: Cards, panels, form rows — the non-flex root every library also ships.

canvas.note: Figma frame, vertical AutoLayout or plain frame

cases.why: The single most common design-system root layout. If this is not carried, nothing is.

canvas.note: Figma AutoLayout HORIZONTAL

cases.why: Chips, tags and inline buttons: the inline sibling of the root layout channel.

canvas.note: Figma AutoLayout HORIZONTAL, hug

cases.why: Legacy layout roots (and display:contents wrappers) still ship in real libraries.

canvas.note: AutoLayout has no table formatting context

cases.why: em-based spacing scales with type; the resolved px is a FUNCTION of an inherited channel.

canvas.note: the resolved px is the canvas truth; the RELATIONSHIP is what is lost

cases.why: Disabled/loading treatments and glass surfaces. Figma has LAYER_BLUR — this IS canvas-expressible.

canvas.note: Figma LAYER_BLUR is an exact match

cases.why: Gap is Figma itemSpacing — the one spacing channel AutoLayout speaks natively.

canvas.note: itemSpacing

cases.why: Two-dimensional grid is the layout Figma AutoLayout cannot express; every data-dense DS ships one.

canvas.note: AutoLayout is 1-D; a 2-D track grid has no canvas spelling

cases.why: Implicit tracks are how card galleries auto-place; the track sizes exist only in the layout engine.

canvas.note: no implicit-track concept on the canvas

cases.why: Fade-out scroll edges. A mask decides visibility just as decisively as a fill.

canvas.note: no mask channel in the emit grammar

cases.construct: @media (min-width: 2000px) branch that does NOT match the pinned viewport
cases.why: Responsive breakpoints. A capture at ONE viewport measures ONE branch and cannot know the others exist.

canvas.note: the OTHER branch is invisible to a single-viewport capture — a whole rendering is missing

cases.why: Button min-widths and container max-widths are the constraint channels Figma has (minWidth/maxWidth).

canvas.note: minWidth on the frame

cases.why: Highlight and overlay treatments. Figma blendMode is an exact match.

canvas.note: Figma blendMode MULTIPLY

cases.construct: a NON-PAINTING element carrying text (display: none)
cases.why: The GENERAL form of the SVG <title> defect: does non-painting text reach the canvas as ink? MEASURED: it is carried, but GUARDED — the promoted part carries declared display:none alongside the text, so the invariant survives. This is the SAFE half of the pair; its twin (visibility:hidden) is not.

canvas.note: INVARIANT HELD: the text is in the contract but the part declares display:none, so nothing draws it

cases.construct: a NON-PAINTING element carrying text (visibility: hidden)
cases.why: visibility:hidden keeps the BOX but paints nothing — the harder half of the SVG <title> invariant. MEASURED: the part is carried with text "INVISIBLE-SENTINEL" and declared display:"block"; the visibility channel is dropped as code-only, so the contract asserts a VISIBLE block containing text the browser paints nowhere. The display:none twin is guarded and safe; this one is not.
cases.expectWhere: anatomy.root.parts.label-2 must carry a non-painting guard, as the display:none twin does

canvas.note: INVARIANT BROKEN: text that paints nowhere is carried with no guard — the SVG <title> defect, generalised

cases.why: Tailwind v4 themes are oklch and Chromium KEEPS the space in computed values.

canvas.note: SOLID fill via the deterministic oklch→sRGB conversion

cases.why: Percentage padding is parent-relative — the captured px is only true at the stage width.

canvas.note: carried as a FIXED px — correct at one width, wrong at every other

cases.why: Badge-on-avatar, focus rings, dropdown carets — the one positioning mode Figma can spell.

canvas.note: absolute child inside a frame

cases.why: Sticky headers, toasts and scrims. Fixed is viewport-relative — a canvas has no viewport.

canvas.note: no viewport-relative positioning on a canvas

cases.why: Sticky table headers. Position depends on scroll state, which no static capture holds.

canvas.note: scroll-dependent placement has no canvas spelling

cases.why: The modal scrim. Native <dialog> is how new libraries ship modals, and the scrim IS the token.

canvas.note: a modal scrim is a real rectangle on the canvas

cases.why: Icon-font glyph pseudo — how Bootstrap/FontAwesome/Material draw carets, chevrons, close ×s.

canvas.note: a glyph from an unavailable icon font has no canvas spelling

cases.why: Fade-out masks and skeleton shimmers are gradient-only pseudos with no box paint.

canvas.note: the v1/v2 decor grammar carries solid paint, not gradient stacks

cases.why: Every list in every documentation-shaped component. The reader has never looked at ::marker.

canvas.note: a list marker would have to be drawn as a real text node

cases.why: Placeholder colour is a REVIEWED design token in every input in every design system.

canvas.note: placeholder text is REAL INK on a canvas mock-up — the loss is visible

cases.why: Selection colour is a themed token in editors and rich-text components.

canvas.note: transient user state; no canvas spelling

cases.why: The modern spelling. A reader that only knows `transform` sees an IDENTITY matrix and reports nothing wrong.

canvas.note: Figma rotation is an exact match — and the box IS rotated on screen

cases.construct: ::part(label) styling across an OPEN shadow boundary
cases.why: The sanctioned theming seam for web components: the page restyles internals it does not own. MEASURED: the shadow-walking reader introduced for the web-components round descends OPEN roots, and getComputedStyle resolves ::part() styling like any other rule — so this is carried. Kept as a case because the carriage is INCIDENTAL (nothing in the pipeline knows what a part() seam IS) and would be lost the moment the walker changed.

canvas.note: the restyled internal is real ink, and it is carried

cases.construct: a custom element with a CLOSED shadow root
cases.why: Closed roots ship in real web-component libraries; the whole rendered box is unreachable from script.

canvas.note: the box is painted and visible; only the READER cannot see it

cases.construct: a captured box exactly equal to the STAGE box (100% × 100%)
cases.why: The GENERAL form of the 100vh-scrim defect: a measured box that is really the harness, not the component.

canvas.note: a stage-sized box is a measurement artefact, not a component fact

cases.why: Half the icon sets in the world ship circles and rects, not paths.

canvas.note: the asset grammar admits path/g only

cases.why: Truncation is in every table cell and menu item; Figma has textTruncation = ENDING.

canvas.note: textTruncation ENDING

cases.why: Chevron flips, loading spinners, checkbox tick scale-ins. Non-identity transforms are everywhere.

canvas.note: the bounded grammar carries translate only

cases.why: Every interactive component declares transitions; they are the design system’s motion tokens.

canvas.note: no canvas spelling — but the channel is a DECLARED fact with its own canvas verdict, which is the honest treatment, not a loss

cases.why: Every library ships fallback chains so a page renders without the theme provider mounted.

canvas.note: text fill; the RESOLVED value is the truth

cases.why: The single-hop token reference: the shape that makes a captured pixel recover its NAME.

canvas.note: variable-bound fill

cases.why: Multi-line truncation. Still the ONLY cross-browser spelling, so every card description uses it.

canvas.note: Figma textTruncation + maxLines is an exact match — this one IS canvas-expressible

cases.why: A disabled input’s grey text: the painted colour is the fill, NOT `color`. Carrying `color` carries a lie.

canvas.note: the text fill IS the ink the canvas draws

cases.why: CJK-capable libraries ship vertical text; the LOGICAL_ALIASES pin assumes horizontal-tb.

canvas.note: Figma AutoLayout has no vertical writing mode
